answer: The farrier enters every horse he shoes in the register, with the shoes nailed and the date of the shoeing. A prism horse shod elsewhere fails the register: at the delta of the shoe the nails must match the farrier's own pattern, and a strange shoeing throws the horse lame. Forging a shoeing means hiring a farrier, shoeing false horses and paying 13,600 in iron and wages, and the relic line in the shoeing register is read at every stable, so a horse whose shoeing was never entered is refused a stall.
